question: Levodopa/carbidopa is an appropriate treatment for drug-induced parkinsonism caused by haloperidol because it replaces the dopamine that haloperidol is blocking.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Levodopa increases dopamine levels, but in DIP the D2 receptors are already blocked by the antipsychotic — more dopamine cannot restore signalling through occupied receptors. Furthermore, levodopa would worsen psychosis by increasing dopaminergic tone in the mesolimbic pathway. The correct treatment is trihexyphenidyl (anticholinergic) — this is an OSCE-examinable prescription.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. Levodopa should never be used for drug-induced parkinsonism. The D2 receptors are pharmacologically blocked by haloperidol — increasing dopamine levels cannot overcome this blockade. Additionally, any dopamine that acts on mesolimbic D2 receptors (which are less occupied) would worsen the psychosis being treated. The correct treatment is an anticholinergic (trihexyphenidyl).
